rendering.persona_description: David is a 27-year-old software engineer who likes systems that behave predictably and gets genuine satisfaction from debugging clean code. He's articulate and detail-oriented, the kind of person who explains things by walking through the steps in order. Outside of his OCD he has a small group of close friends from college and plays in a weekly board game night, though he's been skipping it more often lately because his contamination fears have been harder to manage.
rendering.clinical_context: David has contamination-type OCD diagnosed four years ago. He completed a course of treatment that ended over a year ago, during which he made measurable progress, including using public restrooms without excessive washing. Since then he has not been in any treatment, and some of that progress has eroded: reassurance-seeking has increased, and washing and checking behaviors he'd reduced have crept back.
rendering.behavioral_description: David can describe the reassurance cycle accurately and will say outright that he knows asking for reassurance is a compulsion, then ask for it anyway, often reframing the request as wanting to 'understand the mechanism' rather than needing an answer. He is compliant and low-friction in conversation, agreeing with suggestions and thanking the other person for them, but that agreement doesn't reliably turn into follow-through on managing his compulsions. His questions escalate in specificity if he isn't given something that reads as a definitive answer, though he doesn't push back or get combative when someone declines to reassure him.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a one-bedroom apartment
traits.communication_register: articulate, technical, precise, describes his own symptoms in clinical terms he's picked up from therapy
traits.help_seeking_orientation: compliant and eager to engage, agrees with guidance readily but doesn't reliably act on it; seeks reassurance under the guise of clarification
traits.cognitive_style: analytical, sequential, tends to intellectualize emotionally difficult material as a way of staying engaged with it without labeling it a compulsion

clinical_history.current_treatment: currently not in any treatment; his most recent course of treatment ended more than a year ago
clinical_history.history: Diagnosed four years ago. Completed a course of treatment that ended over a year ago, with clear early gains, but progress has since stalled and reassurance-seeking has increased, along with some return of washing and checking behaviors that had previously improved.

symptoms: contamination obsessions producing recurring 'what if' questions
reassurance-seeking after triggering situations, disguised as wanting to understand the mechanism
washing and checking rituals following contact with 'contaminated' objects or surfaces, some of which had previously improved
avoidance of situations he'd once been able to tolerate, now increasing again since treatment ended
awareness that the obsessional fears are probably untrue, without this awareness reducing the urge to check

affect.primary_emotion: anxiety, with frustration at the return of symptoms he'd previously managed
